I need you to implement GitHub Issue #57: "Improve Grid Appearance and Scale Controls."

Before making any changes, inspect the existing grid implementation, especially the Grid toolbar/menu and code introduced for Issue #56. Also inspect Issue #57's acceptance criteria and understand how the existing grid visibility and snapping functionality works. Do not unnecessarily rewrite or duplicate existing functionality.

Issue #57 requirements:

- Add UI controls for:
  - Grid spacing/scale
  - Grid color
  - Grid transparency/opacity
  - Grid visual layer/depth
- Changes to grid scale or transparency should immediately update the rendered grid without requiring a refresh.
- The grid must remain strictly non-selectable on the workspace.
- Clicking or dragging over grid lines must not select the grid or interfere with selecting/moving other elements.
- The controls should be accessible through the existing Grid toolbar/menu created for Issue #56.
- Do not reimplement the core grid rendering/toggle pipeline or the primary toolbar integration from Issue #56.
- Do not modify the object-to-grid snapping logic beyond what is necessary to support the new configurable snapping distance.

Design decision for this issue:

The grid appearance and scale controls should all be presented together in the existing Grid toolbar menu as a visible list of controls.

Grid spacing and snapping distance should be tied together by default:

- Changing the visible grid spacing should change the snapping distance accordingly.
- There should be a way to disable this relationship.
- When the relationship is disabled, snapping distance should be configurable independently using a relative multiplier/magnitude based on the base grid spacing (for example, 1×, 2×, 0.5×), rather than exposing arbitrary pixel values to the user. This should also be true for the grid, defaulting to 1x size.
- The reason for using relative values is that the visible grid itself provides a natural visual reference. Exact pixel counts would add unnecessary complexity and are not particularly useful to the user.

Do NOT expose exact pixel counts for the grid spacing in the normal UI unless the existing architecture makes this unavoidable.

Implementation expectations:

1. First inspect the relevant existing files and determine the smallest clean set of changes needed.
2. Follow the existing Excalidraw coding patterns, components, atoms/state management, styling, and UI conventions.
3. Preserve existing grid visibility and snapping behavior.
4. Make the new settings update the canvas immediately.
5. Ensure grid rendering remains non-selectable.
6. Add or update meaningful tests for the new behavior, especially:
   - Changing grid spacing updates the rendered grid.
   - Changing opacity/transparency updates the rendered grid.
   - Color changes are applied correctly.
   - Visual layer/depth changes behave correctly.
   - Linked grid/snap spacing updates together.
   - Unlinking them allows independent snap configuration.
   - Existing grid snapping behavior is not broken.
   - The grid cannot be selected as an element.
7. Run the relevant tests after implementation.
8. Run typechecking/linting/formatting if appropriate.
9. Do not modify unrelated files or functionality.
10. Do not commit the changes unless I explicitly ask you to.

Before coding, briefly explain:

- Which files you expect to modify.
- How the existing grid implementation works.
- How you plan to represent the linked/unlinked grid and snapping scales.
- Any ambiguity you find in Issue #57.

Then implement the issue and report:

- Files changed.
- What was implemented.
- Tests added/updated.
- Test results.
- Any remaining concerns or design decisions.

import { useEffect } from "react";

import { EVENT, KEYS, isSelectionLikeTool } from "@excalidraw/common";
import { showSelectedShapeActions } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { NonDeletedExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { actionToggleGridMode, actionToggleGridSnapMode } from "../actions";
import { getShortcutFromShortcutName } from "../actions/shortcuts";
import { atom, useAtom } from "../editor-jotai";
import { t } from "../i18n";

import { useExcalidrawActionManager } from "./App";
import { Island } from "./Island";
import { Switch } from "./Switch";

import "./GridPanel.scss";

import type { AppClassProperties, UIAppState } from "../types";

/** whether the grid settings panel (opened from the extra-tools menu) is open */
export const isGridPanelOpenAtom = atom(false);

/**
 * Opens the grid panel like picking a tool: switches to the selection tool
 * and clears the selection so no other tool or properties panel stays active.
 */
export const openGridPanel = (app: AppClassProperties) => {
  app.setActiveTool({ type: app.state.preferredSelectionTool.type });
  app.setAppState({ selectedElementIds: {}, selectedGroupIds: {} });
  app.updateEditorAtom(isGridPanelOpenAtom, true);
};

/**
 * Left-side panel with the grid toggles, shown after picking "Grid" in the
 * extra-tools menu (like the properties panel shown for the frame tool).
 * Closes when the user switches to another tool, selects or edits elements
 * (anything that brings up the properties panel), or presses Escape.
 */
export const GridPanel = ({
  appState,
  elements,
}: {
  appState: UIAppState;
  elements: readonly NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[];
}) => {
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useAtom(isGridPanelOpenAtom);
  const actionManager = useExcalidrawActionManager();

  // opening the panel switches to the selection tool and clears the
  // selection, so this only becomes true once the user moves on
  const shouldClose =
    !isSelectionLikeTool(appState.activeTool.type) ||
    showSelectedShapeActions(appState, elements);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (shouldClose) {
      setIsOpen(false);
    }
  }, [shouldClose, setIsOpen]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isOpen) {
      return;
    }
    const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (event.key === KEYS.ESCAPE) {
        setIsOpen(false);
      }
    };
    document.addEventListener(EVENT.KEYDOWN, onKeyDown);
    return () => document.removeEventListener(EVENT.KEYDOWN, onKeyDown);
  }, [isOpen, setIsOpen]);

  if (
    !isOpen ||
    shouldClose ||
    appState.viewModeEnabled ||
    !actionManager.isActionEnabled(actionToggleGridMode)
  ) {
    return null;
  }

  return (
    <Island className="GridPanel" padding={2} data-viewport-ui="side">
      <fieldset>
        <legend>{t("toolBar.grid")}</legend>
        <GridPanelToggle
          name="grid-panel-show-grid"
          label={t("labels.showGrid")}
          shortcut={getShortcutFromShortcutName("gridMode")}
          checked={appState.gridModeEnabled}
          onChange={() =>
            actionManager.executeAction(actionToggleGridMode, "ui")
          }
        />
        <GridPanelToggle
          name="grid-panel-snap-to-grid"
          label={t("labels.toggleGridSnap")}
          checked={appState.gridSnapEnabled}
          onChange={() =>
            actionManager.executeAction(actionToggleGridSnapMode, "ui")
          }
        />
      </fieldset>
    </Island>
  );
};

const GridPanelToggle = ({
  name,
  label,
  shortcut,
  checked,
  onChange,
}: {
  name: string;
  label: string;
  shortcut?: string;
  checked: boolean;
  onChange: () => void;
}) => (
  <div className="GridPanel__toggle">
    <label htmlFor={name}>{label}</label>
    {shortcut && <span className="GridPanel__shortcut">{shortcut}</span>}
    <Switch name={name} title={label} checked={checked} onChange={onChange} />
  </div>
);
@use "../css/variables.module" as *;

.excalidraw {
  .GridPanel {
    width: fit-content;
    min-width: 11rem;

    fieldset {
      display: flex;
      flex-direction: column;
      row-gap: 0.5rem;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
      border: none;
    }

    legend {
      margin: 0;
      margin-bottom: 0.25rem;
      padding: 0;
      font-size: 0.75rem;
      color: var(--text-primary-color);
      font-weight: 400;
    }

    &__toggle {
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: space-between;
      column-gap: 1rem;

      label {
        font-size: 0.875rem;
        color: var(--text-primary-color);
        cursor: pointer;
      }
    }

    &__shortcut {
      // keep the shortcut next to the switch, like dropdown menu shortcuts
      margin-inline-start: auto;
      font-size: 0.875rem;
      color: var(--text-primary-color);
      opacity: 0.5;
    }
  }
}

import type {
  StaticCanvasRenderConfig,
  StaticSceneRenderConfig,
} from "../scene/types";
import type { StaticCanvasAppState, Zoom } from "../types";

const GridLineColor = {
  [THEME.LIGHT]: {
    bold: "#dddddd",
    regular: "#e5e5e5",
  },
  [THEME.DARK]: {
    bold: applyDarkModeFilter("#dddddd"),
    regular: applyDarkModeFilter("#e5e5e5"),
  },
} as const;

const strokeGrid = (
  context: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  /** grid cell pixel size */
  gridSize: number,
  /** setting to 1 will disble bold lines */
  gridStep: number,
  scrollX: number,
  scrollY: number,
  zoom: Zoom,
  theme: StaticCanvasRenderConfig["theme"],
  width: number,
  height: number,
) => {
  const offsetX = (scrollX % gridSize) - gridSize;
  const offsetY = (scrollY % gridSize) - gridSize;

  const actualGridSize = gridSize * zoom.value;

  const spaceWidth = 1 / zoom.value;

  context.save();

  // Offset rendering by 0.5 to ensure that 1px wide lines are crisp.
  // We only do this when zoomed to 100% because otherwise the offset is
  // fractional, and also visibly offsets the elements.
  // We also do this per-axis, as each axis may already be offset by 0.5.
  if (zoom.value === 1) {
    context.translate(offsetX % 1 ? 0 : 0.5, offsetY % 1 ? 0 : 0.5);
  }

  // vertical lines
  for (let x = offsetX; x < offsetX + width + gridSize * 2; x += gridSize) {
    const isBold =
      gridStep > 1 && Math.round(x - scrollX) % (gridStep * gridSize) === 0;
    // don't render regular lines when zoomed out and they're barely visible
    if (!isBold && actualGridSize < 10) {
      continue;
    }

    const lineWidth = Math.min(1 / zoom.value, isBold ? 4 : 1);
    context.lineWidth = lineWidth;
    const lineDash = [lineWidth * 3, spaceWidth + (lineWidth + spaceWidth)];

    context.beginPath();
    context.setLineDash(isBold ? [] : lineDash);
    context.strokeStyle = isBold
      ? GridLineColor[theme].bold
      : GridLineColor[theme].regular;
    context.moveTo(x, offsetY - gridSize);
    context.lineTo(x, Math.ceil(offsetY + height + gridSize * 2));
    context.stroke();
  }

  for (let y = offsetY; y < offsetY + height + gridSize * 2; y += gridSize) {
    const isBold =
      gridStep > 1 && Math.round(y - scrollY) % (gridStep * gridSize) === 0;
    if (!isBold && actualGridSize < 10) {
      continue;
    }

    const lineWidth = Math.min(1 / zoom.value, isBold ? 4 : 1);
    context.lineWidth = lineWidth;
    const lineDash = [lineWidth * 3, spaceWidth + (lineWidth + spaceWidth)];

    context.beginPath();
    context.setLineDash(isBold ? [] : lineDash);
    context.strokeStyle = isBold
      ? GridLineColor[theme].bold
      : GridLineColor[theme].regular;
    context.moveTo(offsetX - gridSize, y);
    context.lineTo(Math.ceil(offsetX + width + gridSize * 2), y);
    context.stroke();
  }
  context.restore();
};

  renderConfig: StaticCanvasRenderConfig,
  appState: StaticCanvasAppState,
) => {
  context.translate(frame.x + appState.scrollX, frame.y + appState.scrollY);

import { queryByTestId, queryByText } from "@testing-library/react";

import { CODES, KEYS } from "@excalidraw/common";

import { getShortcutFromShortcutName } from "../actions/shortcuts";
import { isGridPanelOpenAtom } from "../components/GridPanel";
import { editorJotaiStore } from "../editor-jotai";
import { Excalidraw, MainMenu } from "../index";

import { API } from "./helpers/api";
import { Keyboard, UI } from "./helpers/ui";
import { act, fireEvent, render } from "./test-utils";

const { h } = window;

const getGridPanel = () => document.querySelector(".GridPanel");

const getExtraToolsTrigger = () =>
  document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".App-toolbar__extra-tools-trigger")!;

const openExtraToolsMenu = () => {
  fireEvent.click(getExtraToolsTrigger());
  return document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
    ".App-toolbar__extra-tools-dropdown",
  )!;
};

const pickGridFromExtraTools = () => {
  const menu = openExtraToolsMenu();
  fireEvent.click(queryByTestId(menu, "toolbar-grid")!);
};

const getSwitch = (name: string) =>
  document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>(`input[name="${name}"]`)!;

const stubResizeObserver = () => {
  // radix popovers (e.g. the background color picker) need ResizeObserver
  (global as any).ResizeObserver = class ResizeObserver {
    observe() {}
    unobserve() {}
    disconnect() {}
  };
};

beforeEach(() => {
  // the editor jotai store is module-level, so reset the panel between tests
  editorJotaiStore.set(isGridPanelOpenAtom, false);
});

describe("grid panel", () => {
  describe("extra tools menu item", () => {
    beforeEach(async () => {
      await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
    });

    it("should be the first item in More tools, with a G shortcut", () => {
      const menu = openExtraToolsMenu();
      const items = menu.querySelectorAll(".dropdown-menu-item");
      const gridItem = queryByTestId(menu, "toolbar-grid")!;

      expect(items[0]).toBe(gridItem);
      expect(gridItem.textContent).toContain("Grid");
      expect(
        gridItem.querySelector(".dropdown-menu-item__shortcut")?.textContent,
      ).toBe("G");
    });

    it("should open the panel without turning the grid on", () => {
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);

      pickGridFromExtraTools();

      expect(getGridPanel()).not.toBe(null);
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);
      expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(false);
    });

    it("should switch to the selection tool and clear the selection", () => {
      const rectangle = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
      API.setElements([rectangle]);
      API.setSelectedElements([rectangle]);
      UI.clickTool("rectangle");
      expect(h.state.activeTool.type).toBe("rectangle");

      pickGridFromExtraTools();

      expect(h.state.activeTool.type).toBe("selection");
      expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({});
      expect(getGridPanel()).not.toBe(null);
    });

    it("should highlight More tools while the panel is open", () => {
      expect(getExtraToolsTrigger()).not.toHaveClass(
        "App-toolbar__extra-tools-trigger--selected",
      );

      pickGridFromExtraTools();
      expect(getExtraToolsTrigger()).toHaveClass(
        "App-toolbar__extra-tools-trigger--selected",
      );

      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ESCAPE);
      expect(getExtraToolsTrigger()).not.toHaveClass(
        "App-toolbar__extra-tools-trigger--selected",
      );
    });
  });

  describe("panel", () => {
    beforeEach(async () => {
      await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
      pickGridFromExtraTools();
    });

    it("should toggle grid visibility from the Show grid switch", () => {
      const showGrid = getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid");
      expect(showGrid.checked).toBe(false);

      fireEvent.click(showGrid);
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(true);
      expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(false);
      expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid").checked).toBe(true);

      fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid"));
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);
    });

    it("should toggle grid snapping from the Snap to grid switch", () => {
      const snapToGrid = getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid");
      expect(snapToGrid.checked).toBe(false);

      fireEvent.click(snapToGrid);
      expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(true);
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);
      expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid").checked).toBe(true);

      fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid"));
      expect(h.state.gridSnapEnabled).toBe(false);
    });

    it("should reflect grid state changed elsewhere", () => {
      API.setAppState({ gridModeEnabled: true, gridSnapEnabled: true });

      expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid").checked).toBe(true);
      expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid").checked).toBe(true);
    });

    it("should show the Ctrl+' shortcut next to Show grid", () => {
      const showGridRow = getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid").closest(
        ".GridPanel__toggle",
      )!;
      const snapRow = getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid").closest(
        ".GridPanel__toggle",
      )!;

      expect(
        showGridRow.querySelector(".GridPanel__shortcut")?.textContent,
      ).toBe(getShortcutFromShortcutName("gridMode"));
      expect(snapRow.querySelector(".GridPanel__shortcut")).toBe(null);
    });

    it("should update the Show grid switch when using Ctrl+'", () => {
      Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ ctrl: true }, () => {
        Keyboard.codeDown(CODES.QUOTE);
      });

      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(true);
      expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid").checked).toBe(true);
      expect(getGridPanel()).not.toBe(null);
    });

    it("should stay open after toggling a switch", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-show-grid"));
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-snap-to-grid"));
      expect(getGridPanel()).not.toBe(null);
    });

    it("should close on Escape", () => {
      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ESCAPE);
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });

    it("should close when switching to another tool", () => {
      UI.clickTool("rectangle");
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);

      // and stay closed when coming back to the selection tool
      UI.clickTool("selection");
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });

    it("should close when an element gets selected", () => {
      const rectangle = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
      API.setElements([rectangle]);
      act(() => {
        API.setSelectedElements([rectangle]);
      });
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);

      // and stay closed after deselecting
      API.setAppState({ selectedElementIds: {} });
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });

    it("should be hidden in view mode", () => {
      API.setAppState({ viewModeEnabled: true });
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });
  });

  describe("G shortcut", () => {
    beforeEach(async () => {
      stubResizeObserver();
      await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
    });

    it("should toggle the panel with the selection tool and nothing selected", () => {
      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
      expect(getGridPanel()).not.toBe(null);
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(false);

      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });

    it("should keep opening the background picker for fillable tools", () => {
      UI.clickTool("rectangle");

      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);

      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
      expect(h.state.openPopup).toBe("elementBackground");
      expect(h.state.activeTool.type).toBe("rectangle");
    });

    it("should keep opening the background picker for selected fillable elements", () => {
      const rectangle = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
      API.setElements([rectangle]);
      act(() => {
        API.setSelectedElements([rectangle]);
      });

      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);

      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
      expect(h.state.openPopup).toBe("elementBackground");
      expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [rectangle.id]: true });
    });

    it.each([
      ["Shift", { shift: true }],
      ["Alt", { alt: true }],
      ["Ctrl", { ctrl: true }],
      ["Ctrl+Shift", { ctrl: true, shift: true }],
    ])("should not open the panel with %s held", (_, modifiers) => {
      Keyboard.withModifierKeys(modifiers, () => {
        Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
      });
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });

    it("should still group elements with Ctrl+G", () => {
      const rect1 = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 0 });
      const rect2 = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 100 });
      API.setElements([rect1, rect2]);
      act(() => {
        API.setSelectedElements([rect1, rect2]);
      });

      Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ ctrl: true }, () => {
        Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
      });

      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
      expect(h.elements[0].groupIds).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(h.elements[0].groupIds).toEqual(h.elements[1].groupIds);
    });

    it("should not open the panel in view mode", () => {
      API.setAppState({ viewModeEnabled: true });
      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
    });
  });

  describe("gridModeEnabled prop", () => {
    beforeEach(async () => {
      await render(
        <Excalidraw gridModeEnabled={true} handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />,
      );
    });

    it("should hide the Grid item in More tools", () => {
      const menu = openExtraToolsMenu();
      expect(queryByTestId(menu, "toolbar-grid")).toBe(null);
      // the rest of the menu still renders
      expect(queryByTestId(menu, "toolbar-frame")).not.toBe(null);
    });

    it("should ignore the G shortcut", () => {
      const gridModeEnabled = h.state.gridModeEnabled;
      Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.G);
      expect(getGridPanel()).toBe(null);
      expect(h.state.gridModeEnabled).toBe(gridModeEnabled);
    });
  });
});

import type { Scene } from "@excalidraw/element";

import { getNormalizedGridStep } from "../../scene";

import StatsDragInput from "./DragInput";
import { getStepSizedValue } from "./utils";

import type { AppState } from "../../types";

interface PositionProps {
  property: "gridStep";
  scene: Scene;
  appState: AppState;
  setAppState: React.Component<any, AppState>["setState"];
}

const STEP_SIZE = 5;

const CanvasGrid = ({
  property,
  scene,
  appState,
  setAppState,
}: PositionProps) => {
  return (
    <StatsDragInput
      label="Grid step"
      sensitivity={8}
      elements={[]}
      dragInputCallback={({
        nextValue,
        instantChange,
        shouldChangeByStepSize,
        setInputValue,
      }) => {
        setAppState((state) => {
          let nextGridStep;

          if (nextValue) {
            nextGridStep = nextValue;
          } else if (instantChange) {
            nextGridStep = shouldChangeByStepSize
              ? getStepSizedValue(
                  state.gridStep + STEP_SIZE * Math.sign(instantChange),
                  STEP_SIZE,
                )
              : state.gridStep + instantChange;
          }

          if (!nextGridStep) {
            setInputValue(state.gridStep);
            return null;
          }

          nextGridStep = getNormalizedGridStep(nextGridStep);
          setInputValue(nextGridStep);
          return {
            gridStep: nextGridStep,
          };
        });
      }}
      scene={scene}
      value={appState.gridStep}
      property={property}
      appState={appState}
    />
  );
};

export default CanvasGrid;

  public static destroy = () => {
    SnapCache.referenceSnapPoints = null;
    SnapCache.visibleGaps = null;
  };
}

import { RadioButton } from "./RadioButton";

import "./Range.scss";

export type RangeNotch = {
  value: number;

export type RangeProps = {
  label: React.ReactNode;

  notches?: RangeNotch[];
  /** formats the live numeric value shown above the thumb */
  formatValue?: (value: number) => React.ReactNode;
  /** show the value bubble even when value === min (default: hidden at min) */
  alwaysShowValue?: boolean;
};

export const Range = ({
  label,
  value,
  onChange,
  min = 0,
  max = 100,
  step = 10,
  minLabel = min,

  formatValue,
  alwaysShowValue = false,
}: RangeProps) => {
  const rangeRef = React.useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);

  const minLabelRef = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  const displayValue = formatValue ? formatValue(value) : value;
  const showsValue = alwaysShowValue || value !== min;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (rangeRef.current && valueRef.current) {
      const rangeElement = rangeRef.current;
      const valueElement = valueRef.current;
      const inputWidth = rangeElement.offsetWidth;
      const thumbWidth =
        parseFloat(
          getComputedStyle(rangeElement).getPropertyValue(
            "--slider-thumb-size",
          ),
        ) || 16;
      const progress = ((value - min) / (max - min || 1)) * 100;
      const position =
        (progress / 100) * (inputWidth - thumbWidth) + thumbWidth / 2;
      valueElement.style.left = `${position}px`;
      rangeElement.style.background = `linear-gradient(to right, var(--color-slider-track) 0%, var(--color-slider-track) ${progress}%, var(--button-bg) ${progress}%, var(--button-bg) 100%)`;
    }

    if (valueRef.current && minLabelRef.current) {
      const minLabelElement = minLabelRef.current;
      // hide the min-value tick label whenever the value bubble would render
      // on top of (or right next to) it, so the two never overlap
      const overlapping =
        showsValue &&

import clsx from "clsx";

import { RadioButton } from "./RadioButton";

import type { JSX } from "react";

export const RadioSelection = <T extends Object>(
  props: {
    options: {
      value: T;
      text: string;
      icon: JSX.Element;
      testId?: string;
      /** if not supplied, defaults to value identity check */
      active?: boolean;
    }[];
    value: T | null;
    type?: "radio" | "button";
  } & (
    | { type?: "radio"; group: string; onChange: (value: T) => void }
    | {
        type: "button";
        onClick: (
          value: T,
          event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement, MouseEvent>,
        ) => void;
      }
  ),
) => (
  <>
    {props.options.map((option) =>
      props.type === "button" ? (
        <RadioButton
          key={option.text}
          icon={option.icon}
          title={option.text}
          testId={option.testId}
          active={option.active ?? props.value === option.value}
          onClick={(event) => props.onClick(option.value, event)}
        />
      ) : (
        <label
          key={option.text}
          className={clsx({ active: props.value === option.value })}
          title={option.text}
        >
          <input
            type="radio"
            name={props.group}
            onChange={() => props.onChange(option.value)}
            checked={props.value === option.value}
            data-testid={option.testId}
          />
          {option.icon}
        </label>
      ),
    )}
  </>
);

export const ColorPicker = ({
  type,
  color,
  onChange,
  label,
  elements,
  palette = COLOR_PALETTE,
  topPicks,
  updateData,
  appState,
  allowGradient,
}: ColorPickerProps) => {
  const openRef = useRef(appState.openPopup);
  useEffect(() => {
    openRef.current = appState.openPopup;
  }, [appState.openPopup]);
  const stylesPanelMode = useStylesPanelMode();
  const isCompactMode = stylesPanelMode !== "full";

  return (
    <div>
      <div
        role="dialog"
        aria-modal="true"
        className={clsx("color-picker-container", {
          "color-picker-container--no-top-picks": isCompactMode,
        })}
      >
        {!isCompactMode && (
          <TopPicks
            activeColor={color}
            onChange={onChange}
            type={type}
            topPicks={topPicks}
          />
        )}
        {!isCompactMode && <ButtonSeparator />}
        <Popover.Root
          open={appState.openPopup === type}
          onOpenChange={(open) => {
            if (open) {
              updateData({ openPopup: type });
            }
          }}
        >
          {/* serves as an active color indicator as well */}
          <ColorPickerTrigger
            color={color}
            label={label}
            type={type}
            mode={type === "elementStroke" ? "stroke" : "background"}
            editingTextElement={!!appState.editingTextElement}
            onToggle={() => {
              // atomic switch: if another popup is open, close it first, then open this one next tick
              if (appState.openPopup === type) {
                // toggle off on same trigger
                updateData({ openPopup: null });
              } else if (appState.openPopup) {
                updateData({ openPopup: type });
              } else {
                // open this one
                updateData({ openPopup: type });
              }
            }}
          />
          {/* popup content */}
          {appState.openPopup === type && (
            <ColorPickerPopupContent
              type={type}
              color={color}
              onChange={onChange}
              label={label}
              elements={elements}
              palette={palette}
              updateData={updateData}
              getOpenPopup={() => openRef.current}
              appState={appState}
              allowGradient={allowGradient}
            />
          )}
        </Popover.Root>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};
import clsx from "clsx";

import {
  COLOR_OUTLINE_CONTRAST_THRESHOLD,
  DEFAULT_CANVAS_BACKGROUND_PICKS,
  DEFAULT_ELEMENT_BACKGROUND_PICKS,
  DEFAULT_ELEMENT_STROKE_PICKS,
  isColorDark,
} from "@excalidraw/common";

import type { ColorPickerType } from "./colorPickerUtils";

interface TopPicksProps {
  onChange: (color: string) => void;
  type: ColorPickerType;
  activeColor: string | null;
  topPicks?: readonly string[];
}

export const TopPicks = ({
  onChange,
  type,
  activeColor,
  topPicks,
}: TopPicksProps) => {
  let colors;
  if (type === "elementStroke") {
    colors = DEFAULT_ELEMENT_STROKE_PICKS;
  }

  if (type === "elementBackground") {
    colors = DEFAULT_ELEMENT_BACKGROUND_PICKS;
  }

  if (type === "canvasBackground") {
    colors = DEFAULT_CANVAS_BACKGROUND_PICKS;
  }

  // this one can overwrite defaults
  if (topPicks) {
    colors = topPicks;
  }

  if (!colors) {
    console.error("Invalid type for TopPicks");
    return null;
  }

  return (
    <div className="color-picker__top-picks">
      {colors.map((color: string) => (
        <button
          className={clsx("color-picker__button", {
            active: color === activeColor,
            "is-transparent": color === "transparent" || !color,
            "has-outline": !isColorDark(
              color,
              COLOR_OUTLINE_CONTRAST_THRESHOLD,
            ),
          })}
          style={{ "--swatch-color": color }}
          key={color}
          type="button"
          title={color}
          onClick={() => onChange(color)}
          data-testid={`color-top-pick-${color}`}
        >
          <div className="color-picker__button-outline" />
        </button>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
};

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-08 21:20:54Z)**_

I have enough context. Here's the plan before coding.

**How the existing grid works**

- State: `gridSize` (px, default 20), `gridStep` (bold line every N cells), `gridModeEnabled` (visibility), `gridSnapEnabled` (snapping) in `AppState`, persisted via `APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF` and normalized in `restore.ts`.
- Rendering: `strokeGrid()` in [staticScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts) paints lines onto the **static canvas** before elements; `StaticCanvas` re-renders when its memoized appState slice (`gridSize`, `gridStep`, …) changes.
- Snapping: everything goes through `App.getEffectiveGridSize()` (returns `gridSize` when snapping is on), except one direct `appState.gridSize` read in [binding.ts:846](packages/element/src/binding.ts#L846).
- Issue #56 added `GridPanel` (an `Island` opened from More tools / `G`) with Show grid / Snap to grid switches.
- The grid isn't an element. It's only pixels on the static canvas, and the interactive canvas above it takes all pointer events, so it can't be hit-tested or selected.

**Representation**

- `gridSize` stays the **base** spacing (public API, persisted, untouched).
- New state: `gridScale` (multiplier, default 1), `gridSnapLinked` (default true), `gridSnapScale` (multiplier, default 1), `gridColor`, `gridOpacity` (0–100), `gridLayer: "below" | "above"`.
- Visible spacing = `gridSize × gridScale`. Snap spacing = `gridSize × (linked ? gridScale : gridSnapScale)`. Both use shared helpers in `@excalidraw/common`, so `getEffectiveGridSize()` and `binding.ts` pick them up with no changes to the snapping algorithms.
- When you unlink, `gridSnapScale` starts at the current `gridScale`, so snapping doesn't jump.

**Files I expect to change:** `common/constants.ts`, `common/points.ts`, `types.ts`, `appState.ts`, `restore.ts`, `scene/normalize.ts`, `staticScene.ts`, `StaticCanvas.tsx`, `App.tsx` (one line), `binding.ts` (one line), `GridPanel.tsx/.scss`, `ColorPicker/colorPickerUtils.ts` (add a `gridColor` picker type), `actionCanvas.tsx` (keep settings on clear), `en.json`, plus tests.

**Ambiguities in #57**

- "Relative to base grid spacing": I read the snap multiplier as relative to the **base** `gridSize`, not the scaled grid. Otherwise unlinking wouldn't separate the two.
- "Visual layer/depth": I read this as drawing the grid behind elements (default) or on top of them.
- What happens to the snap value when you re-link: I keep the stored snap multiplier but ignore it while linked.

Starting implementation.

  for (const [key, defaultValue] of Object.entries(defaultAppState) as [
    keyof typeof defaultAppState,
    any,

    // if AppState contains a legacy key, prefer that one and migrate its
    // value to the new one
    const suppliedValue = appState[key];

    const localValue = localAppState ? localAppState[key] : undefined;
    (nextAppState as any)[key] =
      suppliedValue !== undefined
        ? suppliedValue
        : localValue !== undefined
        ? localValue
        : defaultValue;
  }

  const boxSelectionMode =
    appState.boxSelectionMode ?? localAppState?.boxSelectionMode;
  if (boxSelectionMode !== undefined) {
    nextAppState.boxSelectionMode = boxSelectionMode;
  }

  // grid snapping used to be implied by `gridModeEnabled`, so preserve that
  // behavior for data saved before `gridSnapEnabled` existed
  if (
    appState.gridSnapEnabled === undefined &&
    localAppState?.gridSnapEnabled === undefined
  ) {
    nextAppState.gridSnapEnabled = nextAppState.gridModeEnabled;
  }

  // legacy: `currentItemStrokeWidthKey` ("thin" | "medium" | "bold") predates
  // the numeric currentItemStrokeWidth slider value
  const legacyStrokeWidthKey = (appState as any).currentItemStrokeWidthKey;
  const strokeWidth =
    typeof legacyStrokeWidthKey === "string" &&
    legacyStrokeWidthKey in STROKE_WIDTH
      ? STROKE_WIDTH[legacyStrokeWidthKey as keyof typeof STROKE_WIDTH]
      : nextAppState.currentItemStrokeWidth;

  // clamp in case an old/corrupted export carries an out-of-range numeric value
  nextAppState.currentItemStrokeWidth = isFiniteNumber(strokeWidth)
    ? clamp(strokeWidth, MIN_STROKE_WIDTH, MAX_STROKE_WIDTH)
    : defaultAppState.currentItemStrokeWidth;

}

const GridScaleSelection = ({
  group,
  options,
  value,
  onChange,
}: {
  group: string;
  options: number[];
  value: number;
  onChange: (value: number) => void;
}) => (
  <div className="buttonList GridPanel__scales">
    <RadioSelection<number>
      group={group}
      options={options.map((scale) => ({
        value: scale,
        text: \`\${scale}×\`,
        icon: <span>{scale}×</span>,
        testId: \`\${group}-\${scale}\`,
      }))}
      value={value}
      onChange={onChange}
    />
  </div>
);
`],
];

describe("grid appearance and scale", () => {
  const mouse = new Pointer("mouse");

  type CanvasEvent = { type: string; props: Record<string, any> };

  const getStaticContext = () =>
    document
      .querySelector<HTMLCanvasElement>("canvas.static")!
      .getContext("2d") as unknown as {
      __getEvents: () => CanvasEvent[];
      __clearEvents: () => void;
    };

  /** canvas events recorded while running \`fn\` (i.e. the re-render it caused) */
  const getRenderEvents = (fn: () => void) => {
    const context = getStaticContext();
    context.__clearEvents();
    act(fn);
    return context.__getEvents();
  };

  /** spacing between the first two grid lines drawn (scene px at 100% zoom) */
  const getRenderedGridSpacing = (events: CanvasEvent[]) => {
    const [first, second] = events.filter((event) => event.type === "moveTo");
    return second.props.x - first.props.x;
  };

  const getStrokeStyles = (events: CanvasEvent[]) =>
    new Set(
      events
        .filter((event) => event.type === "strokeStyle")
        .map((event) => event.props.value),
    );

  const getPanelButton = (testId: string) =>
    queryByTestId(document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".GridPanel")!, testId)!;

  beforeEach(async () => {
    mouse.reset();
    await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
    API.setAppState({ gridModeEnabled: true });
    pickGridFromExtraTools();
  });

  describe("defaults", () => {
    it("should render the grid like before, at 1× with the default color", () => {
      expect(h.state.gridScale).toBe(1);
      expect(h.state.gridSnapLinked).toBe(true);
      expect(h.state.gridSnapScale).toBe(1);
      expect(h.state.gridColor).toBe(DEFAULT_GRID_COLOR);
      expect(h.state.gridOpacity).toBe(100);
      expect(h.state.gridLayer).toBe("below");

      const events = getRenderEvents(() => {
        API.setAppState({ scrollX: 1 });
      });
      expect(getRenderedGridSpacing(events)).toBe(h.state.gridSize);
      expect(getStrokeStyles(events)).toEqual(new Set(["#dddddd", "#e5e5e5"]));
      expect(
        events.some(
          (event) => event.type === "globalAlpha" && event.props.value !== 1,
        ),
      ).toBe(false);
    });

    it("should mark the 1× options as active", () => {
      expect(
        getPanelButton("grid-panel-grid-scale-1") as HTMLInputElement,
      ).toBeChecked();
      expect(getSwitch("grid-panel-link-snap").checked).toBe(true);
      // snap distance follows the grid while linked
      expect(getPanelButton("grid-panel-snap-scale-1")).toBe(null);
    });
  });

  describe("grid size", () => {
    it.each([0.5, 1, 2, 4])(
      "should immediately render the grid at %s× the base size",
      (scale) => {
        const events = getRenderEvents(() => {
          fireEvent.click(getPanelButton(`grid-panel-grid-scale-${scale}`));
        });

        expect(h.state.gridScale).toBe(scale);
        // base size is untouched, only the multiplier changes
        expect(h.state.gridSize).toBe(20);
        if (scale !== 1) {
          expect(getRenderedGridSpacing(events)).toBe(20 * scale);
        }
      },
    );

    it("should not expose pixel values in the panel", () => {
      const panel = document.querySelector(".GridPanel")!;
      expect(panel.textContent).not.toMatch(/\dpx/);
      expect(panel.querySelector('input[type="number"]')).toBe(null);
    });
  });

  describe("color", () => {
    it("should apply a picked color to the rendered grid", () => {
      const color = COLOR_PALETTE.red[1];
      const events = getRenderEvents(() => {
        fireEvent.click(getPanelButton(`color-top-pick-${color}`));
      });

      expect(h.state.gridColor).toBe(color);
      expect(getStrokeStyles(events)).toEqual(new Set([color]));
    });

    it("should apply the dark mode filter to a custom color", () => {
      const color = COLOR_PALETTE.blue[1];
      API.setAppState({ theme: THEME.DARK });

      const events = getRenderEvents(() => {
        API.setAppState({ gridColor: color });
      });

      expect(getStrokeStyles(events)).toEqual(
        new Set([applyDarkModeFilter(color)]),
      );
    });
  });

  describe("opacity", () => {
    it("should immediately render the grid with the chosen opacity", () => {
      const events = getRenderEvents(() => {
        fireEvent.change(getPanelButton("grid-panel-opacity"), {
          target: { value: "40" },
        });
      });

      expect(h.state.gridOpacity).toBe(40);
      expect(events).toContainEqual(
        expect.objectContaining({
          type: "globalAlpha",
          props: expect.objectContaining({ value: 0.4 }),
        }),
      );
    });

    it("should not affect element opacity", () => {
      const rectangle = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", opacity: 100 });
      API.setElements([rectangle]);

      fireEvent.change(getPanelButton("grid-panel-opacity"), {
        target: { value: "40" },
      });

      expect(h.elements[0].opacity).toBe(100);
      expect(h.state.currentItemOpacity).toBe(100);
    });
  });

  describe("layer", () => {
    const getLayerOrder = (events: CanvasEvent[]) => {
      const gridIndex = events.findIndex(
        (event) => event.type === "strokeStyle",
      );
      const elementIndex = events.findIndex(
        (event) => event.type === "drawImage",
      );
      expect(gridIndex).not.toBe(-1);
      expect(elementIndex).not.toBe(-1);
      return gridIndex < elementIndex ? "below" : "above";
    };

    beforeEach(() => {
      API.setElements([
        API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 10, y: 10, width: 100 }),
      ]);
    });

    it("should render the grid below the elements by default", () => {
      const events = getRenderEvents(() => {
        API.setAppState({ scrollX: 1 });
      });
      expect(getLayerOrder(events)).toBe("below");
    });

    it("should render the grid above the elements when chosen", () => {
      const events = getRenderEvents(() => {
        fireEvent.click(getPanelButton("grid-panel-layer-above"));
      });
      expect(h.state.gridLayer).toBe("above");
      expect(getLayerOrder(events)).toBe("above");

      const eventsBelow = getRenderEvents(() => {
        fireEvent.click(getPanelButton("grid-panel-layer-below"));
      });
      expect(h.state.gridLayer).toBe("below");
      expect(getLayerOrder(eventsBelow)).toBe("below");
    });
  });

  describe("snapping distance", () => {
    /** drags a 100×100 rectangle at the origin by (dx, dy) */
    const dragRectangleBy = (dx: number, dy: number) => {
      const rectangle = API.createElement({
        type: "rectangle",
        x: 0,
        y: 0,
        width: 100,
        height: 100,
        backgroundColor: COLOR_PALETTE.red[1],
        fillStyle: "solid",
      });
      API.setElements([rectangle]);

      mouse.downAt(50, 50);
      mouse.moveTo(50 + dx, 50 + dy);
      mouse.upAt();

      return h.elements[0];
    };

    beforeEach(() => {
      API.setAppState({ gridSnapEnabled: true });
    });

    it("should keep snapping to the base grid by default", () => {
      expect(h.app.getEffectiveGridSize()).toBe(20);

      const rectangle = dragRectangleBy(27, 27);
      expect([rectangle.x, rectangle.y]).toEqual([20, 20]);
    });

    it("should change the snapping distance together with the grid size", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getPanelButton("grid-panel-grid-scale-2"));

      expect(h.state.gridSnapLinked).toBe(true);
      expect(h.app.getEffectiveGridSize()).toBe(40);

      const rectangle = dragRectangleBy(27, 27);
      expect([rectangle.x, rectangle.y]).toEqual([40, 40]);
    });

    it("should allow an independent snap distance once unlinked", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getPanelButton("grid-panel-grid-scale-2"));
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-link-snap"));

      // unlinking keeps the current distance so snapping doesn't jump
      expect(h.state.gridSnapLinked).toBe(false);
      expect(h.state.gridSnapScale).toBe(2);
      expect(h.app.getEffectiveGridSize()).toBe(40);
      expect(
        getPanelButton("grid-panel-snap-scale-2") as HTMLInputElement,
      ).toBeChecked();

      fireEvent.click(getPanelButton("grid-panel-snap-scale-0.5"));
      expect(h.state.gridSnapScale).toBe(0.5);
      expect(h.app.getEffectiveGridSize()).toBe(10);
      // the rendered grid stays where it was
      expect(h.state.gridScale).toBe(2);

      // and changing the grid no longer affects snapping
      fireEvent.click(getPanelButton("grid-panel-grid-scale-4"));
      expect(h.app.getEffectiveGridSize()).toBe(10);

      const rectangle = dragRectangleBy(27, 27);
      expect([rectangle.x, rectangle.y]).toEqual([30, 30]);
    });

    it("should follow the grid size again when relinked", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-link-snap"));
      fireEvent.click(getPanelButton("grid-panel-snap-scale-0.25"));
      expect(h.app.getEffectiveGridSize()).toBe(5);

      fireEvent.click(getSwitch("grid-panel-link-snap"));
      fireEvent.click(getPanelButton("grid-panel-grid-scale-0.5"));

      expect(h.state.gridSnapLinked).toBe(true);
      expect(h.app.getEffectiveGridSize()).toBe(10);
      expect(getPanelButton("grid-panel-snap-scale-0.25")).toBe(null);
    });

    it("should not snap when grid snapping is off, regardless of scale", () => {
      fireEvent.click(getPanelButton("grid-panel-grid-scale-2"));
      API.setAppState({ gridSnapEnabled: false });

      expect(h.app.getEffectiveGridSize()).toBe(null);
      const rectangle = dragRectangleBy(27, 27);
      expect([rectangle.x, rectangle.y]).toEqual([27, 27]);
    });
  });

  describe("non-selectable grid", () => {
    beforeEach(() => {
      API.setAppState({ gridLayer: "above" });
    });

    it.each(["below", "above"] as const)(
      "should not select anything when clicking a grid line (%s elements)",
      (gridLayer) => {
        API.setAppState({ gridLayer });
        // a grid line intersection
        mouse.clickAt(40, 40);

        expect(h.elements).toEqual([]);
        expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({});
      },
    );

    it("should select and move elements under grid lines drawn above them", () => {
      const rectangle = API.createElement({
        type: "rectangle",
        x: 0,
        y: 0,
        width: 100,
        height: 100,
        backgroundColor: COLOR_PALETTE.red[1],
        fillStyle: "solid",
      });
      API.setElements([rectangle]);

      // grid lines cross the rectangle at x/y = 20, 40, …
      mouse.downAt(40, 40);
      mouse.moveTo(70, 90);
      mouse.upAt();

      expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [rectangle.id]: true });
      expect([h.elements[0].x, h.elements[0].y]).toEqual([30, 50]);
      expect(h.elements).toHaveLength(1);
    });

    it("should box-select elements when dragging across grid lines", () => {
      const rectangle = API.createElement({
        type: "rectangle",
        x: 100,
        y: 100,
        width: 40,
        height: 40,
      });
      API.setElements([rectangle]);

      mouse.downAt(80, 80);
      mouse.moveTo(160, 160);
      mouse.upAt();

      expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [rectangle.id]: true });
    });

    it("should not add the grid to select all", () => {
      const rectangle = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle" });
      API.setElements([rectangle]);

      Keyboard.withModifierKeys({ ctrl: true }, () => {
        Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.A);
      });

      expect(h.elements).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [rectangle.id]: true });
    });
  });
});

describe("grid appearance restore", () => {

    const appState = restoreAppState(
      {
        gridScale: 100,
        gridSnapScale: -1,
        gridSnapLinked: "yes" as any,
        gridColor: 5 as any,

Root causes: jsdom reports a 0×0 viewport, so elements are culled before drawing; box-select needs the same intermediate pointer move the existing selection tests use. Fixing the tests:

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-08 21:33:48Z)**_

I've implemented Issue #57: the Grid panel from #56 now holds all the new controls, and every change redraws the grid immediately. Typecheck, ESLint and Prettier are clean, and the full test suite passes (123 files, 1802 tests). I haven't opened the panel in a browser, so its spacing and button sizing are checked only by tests, not by eye. Nothing is committed.

**How the existing grid works**

- **Settings:** stored as `gridSize` (base spacing in px, default 20), `gridStep` (bold line every N cells), `gridModeEnabled` (visible) and `gridSnapEnabled` (snapping).
- **Drawing:** `strokeGrid()` paints the lines onto the bottom canvas (the static canvas), before the elements.
- **Snapping:** almost everything gets the snap distance from `App.getEffectiveGridSize()`. One spot in [binding.ts](packages/element/src/binding.ts) read `appState.gridSize` directly.
- **Why it can't be selected:** the grid isn't an element. It's just pixels on the static canvas, and the canvas above it receives all clicks.

**How linked/unlinked scales are represented**

- `gridSize` keeps its meaning as the base spacing, so saved files and apps that embed the editor are unaffected.
- New settings: `gridScale` (default 1×), `gridSnapLinked` (default on), `gridSnapScale` (1×), `gridColor`, `gridOpacity` (0–100) and `gridLayer` (`"below"` / `"above"`).
- Visible spacing is base × `gridScale`. Snap distance is base × `gridScale` while linked, and base × `gridSnapScale` once unlinked.
- Two shared helpers in [points.ts](packages/common/src/points.ts) compute these. `getEffectiveGridSize()` and the one line in `binding.ts` now call them; the snapping logic itself is unchanged.

**Panel controls** ([GridPanel.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx)), below the existing Show grid / Snap to grid switches:

- **Grid size:** 0.5× / 1× / 2× / 4× buttons.
- **"Snap to grid size" switch** (on by default). Turning it off shows a **Snap distance** row: 0.25× / 0.5× / 1× / 2× / 4×.
- **Grid color:** the same quick-pick color picker as the canvas background, plus a hex field. I added a `gridColor` picker type for this.
- **Grid opacity:** a slider from 10–100%.
- **Grid layer:** "Behind elements" / "Above elements".
- No pixel values appear anywhere in the panel.

**Other changes:** settings are saved and restored (invalid values are clamped or reset to defaults), Clear canvas keeps them, and the canvas redraws when any of them change.

**Tests:** 25 new tests in [gridPanel.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/gridPanel.test.tsx). They check the actual canvas draw calls for:

- **Spacing:** each scale changes the line spacing.
- **Color:** a picked color is applied, including in dark mode.
- **Opacity:** the grid's opacity changes and element opacity doesn't.
- **Layer:** the grid is drawn before or after the elements as chosen.
- **Defaults:** the out-of-the-box grid draws exactly as before.
- **Snapping, linked and unlinked:** dragging a rectangle checks the snap result in both modes, plus re-linking and snapping turned off.
- **Selection:** clicking or dragging on grid lines selects or creates nothing, with the grid behind or above. Elements under the grid can still be selected, moved and box-selected, and select-all only picks real elements.
- **Restore:** invalid saved settings are cleaned up.

I also refreshed 5 snapshot files. I checked the diff: it only adds the six new settings to 133 saved-state snapshots, plus one SVG export whose embedded scene now includes them. No render counts or other values changed.

**Interpretations and decisions to review:**

- **"Relative to base spacing":** I took the snap multiplier to be relative to the base `gridSize`, not the scaled grid. Otherwise unlinking couldn't make the two independent.
- **Unlinking** starts the snap value at the current grid scale, so snapping doesn't jump. Re-linking keeps the stored snap value but ignores it while linked.
- **"Layer/depth":** I took this to mean behind elements (the default) or on top of them. "On top" can't cover embedded web content (iframes), because those sit above the canvas.
- **Grid size has no 0.25×.** At that size the existing renderer hides lines thinner than 10px on screen, so only every fifth line would show. Snap distance does offer 0.25×.
- **Color:** the default color keeps the original look exactly (regular lines are a slightly lighter shade than bold ones). A custom color applies to both kinds of line, which still differ by being dashed and thinner.
- **Escape** closes the whole Grid panel even when its color popup is open. That's how the #56 panel already handles Escape.

The `.specstory/history/...` file in your working tree is being written by the SpecStory extension, not by me, so I left it alone.

You're right on points 1 and 2. I should have stopped after the plan and waited for your go-ahead. Since then I've only investigated; nothing has changed.

# Part A — What the current changes do

There are four chains. Each starts where a value is stored and ends where it has an effect.

**Chain 1 — New grid settings (stored state)**

1. [types.ts](packages/excalidraw/types.ts) declares six new fields on `AppState`: `gridScale`, `gridSnapLinked`, `gridSnapScale`, `gridColor`, `gridOpacity`, `gridLayer`. It also adds four of them to `StaticCanvasAppState`, the slice of state the canvas renderer is allowed to see.
2. [appState.ts:76-81](packages/excalidraw/appState.ts#L76-L81) sets their defaults (1×, linked, 1×, `#dddddd`, 100, `"below"`). [appState.ts:213-218](packages/excalidraw/appState.ts#L213-L218) marks them as saved to the browser and to exported files.
3. [restore.ts:1259-1282](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts#L1259-L1282) cleans the values when a file or local storage is loaded. It uses clamps in [normalize.ts](packages/excalidraw/scene/normalize.ts), which use `MIN/MAX_GRID_SCALE` from [constants.ts:238-239](packages/common/src/constants.ts#L238-L239).
4. [actionCanvas.tsx](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionCanvas.tsx) keeps these settings when you use "Clear canvas".

**Chain 2 — Drawing the grid**

1. [StaticCanvas.tsx:96-99](packages/excalidraw/components/canvases/StaticCanvas.tsx#L96-L99) adds the four visual fields to the list it compares between renders. Without this, changing a setting would never redraw the canvas, so this is what makes changes appear instantly.
2. That list reaches `_renderStaticScene` in [staticScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts):
   - [Line 286](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L286) wraps the grid drawing in `renderGridLayer`, which uses `getGridSpacing()` from [points.ts:72](packages/common/src/points.ts#L72) (base `gridSize` × `gridScale`).
   - The grid is drawn either before the elements ([line 303](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L303)) or after them ([line 511](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L511)), depending on `gridLayer`. Both cases stay on the static canvas, which never receives clicks, so the grid can't be selected.
   - `strokeGrid` gets the color through `getGridLineColor` ([line 59](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L59)), which applies the dark-mode filter. Opacity is applied with `globalAlpha` ([line 97](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L97)).

**Chain 3 — Snapping**

1. `getGridSnapSpacing()` in [points.ts:80](packages/common/src/points.ts#L80) returns base × `gridScale` while linked, and base × `gridSnapScale` once unlinked.
2. Two places use it:
   - [App.tsx:1372](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L1372), `getEffectiveGridSize()`. Every snapping code path (dragging, resizing, arrows, arrow keys, text placement) already goes through this method, so changing it covers all of them.
   - [binding.ts:847](packages/element/src/binding.ts#L847), the one place that read `appState.gridSize` directly.

**Chain 4 — The panel** [GridPanel.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx) writes each setting with `useExcalidrawSetAppState()`, which then drives Chains 2 and 3. It contains:

- Grid size buttons (line 135)
- The link switch
- Snap distance buttons, shown only when unlinked (line 159)
- `ColorPicker` with `palette={null}` (line 169–170)
- An opacity `Range` (line 181)
- Layer buttons

Supporting changes:

- A `"gridColor"` value added to the color picker types in [colorPickerUtils.ts](packages/excalidraw/components/ColorPicker/colorPickerUtils.ts) and to `openPopup` in `types.ts`. A matching branch in [Picker.tsx:79](packages/excalidraw/components/ColorPicker/Picker.tsx#L79) was needed to satisfy the type checker.
- Strings in [en.json](packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json) and styles in [GridPanel.scss](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.scss).

**Tests:** I added 401 lines to [gridPanel.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/gridPanel.test.tsx). I also regenerated 5 snapshot files; those changes only add the six new settings to stored-state snapshots.

# Part B — Proposed fixes (not yet implemented)

### Fix 1 — Remove the tests

- Run `git checkout -- packages/excalidraw/tests/gridPanel.test.tsx`. This restores the file exactly as Issue #56 left it.
- **Decision needed on the 5 snapshot files.** They're regenerated data, not test cases I wrote. If I revert them too, about 133 existing tests will fail until they're regenerated, because the stored state now has six more fields.
- I recommend keeping them so the suite stays green, and reverting only `gridPanel.test.tsx`. I'll revert them as well if you prefer.

### Fix 2 — The opacity slider is invisible

- **Root cause:**
  - [Range.tsx:70](packages/excalidraw/components/Range.tsx#L70) paints the slider track with a gradient that uses the CSS variable `var(--button-bg)`.
  - That variable is only defined for the properties panel (`.App-menu__left`, [styles.scss:732-742](packages/excalidraw/css/styles.scss#L732-L742)).
  - The Grid panel is rendered next to it, not inside it ([LayerUI.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/LayerUI.tsx), the `App-menu_top__left` container). Inside the Grid panel the variable is undefined, which makes the whole gradient invalid, so the track renders transparent.
- **Fix:** in [GridPanel.scss](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.scss), define `--button-bg` (and `--button-border`) on `.GridPanel`, plus the dark-theme values, copying the properties panel's light and dark definitions.
- **Why here:** the fix stays inside the panel's own stylesheet. It doesn't touch global styles or `Range`, which other panels use.

### Fix 3 — A slider plus preset buttons for grid size and snap distance (0.25×–8×, steps of 0.05)

- **[constants.ts:239](packages/common/src/constants.ts#L239):** raise `MAX_GRID_SCALE` from 4 to 8. This one change flows into the clamp in `getNormalizedGridScale` ([normalize.ts:25](packages/excalidraw/scene/normalize.ts#L25)) and then into the restore code ([restore.ts:1259](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts#L1259)), so saved 8× values survive a reload.
- **Add `GRID_SCALE_STEP = 0.05`** next to it.
- **[GridPanel.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx):** replace the `GridScaleSelection` button row (lines 135, 159, 218) with the existing `Range` component's `notches` feature. Line widths in the properties panel use the same pattern ([actionProperties.tsx:627](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionProperties.tsx#L627)): one control with preset buttons above a slider.
  - Both controls use `min=0.25`, `max=8`, `step=0.05`.
  - Presets are 0.25×, 0.5×, 1×, 2×, 4×, 8×. The two option arrays (lines 37–38) become one list.
  - The value shows as "1.35×", never as pixels.
  - Chain: the slider's `onChange` → `setAppState({ gridScale })` → Chain 2 redraws the grid. While linked, it also changes snapping through `getGridSnapSpacing` in Chain 3. The snap slider writes `gridSnapScale`, which only Chain 3 reads.
- **Rounding:** values are rounded to 2 decimals in the `onChange` handler, so floating-point leftovers (e.g. 1.1500000001) never get into stored state.
- **[GridPanel.scss](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.scss):** style the preset buttons to fit their text ("0.25×" won't fit the default square icon button). Widen the panel's `max-width` from 14rem to about 16rem so six buttons fit on one row.

### Fix 4 — The full color picker, without gradients

- **[GridPanel.tsx:169-170](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx#L169-L170):** drop `palette={null}`. `ColorPicker` then uses its default `COLOR_PALETTE` and renders the same `Picker` the stroke color uses: palette colors, shades, hex input and eyedropper.
  - Gradient stays off because `allowGradient` defaults to false, and the gradient button only appears for `elementBackground` ([Picker.tsx:215](packages/excalidraw/components/ColorPicker/Picker.tsx#L215)).
  - The quick picks (`GRID_COLOR_PICKS`) stay as the swatch row.
- **[Picker.tsx:79](packages/excalidraw/components/ColorPicker/Picker.tsx#L79):** the "Custom colors" section is currently empty for the grid. I propose filling it with the scene's most-used stroke colors, by passing `"elementStroke"` to `getMostUsedCustomColors` when the type is `gridColor`. That makes it match the stroke picker. The alternative is leaving it empty, as the canvas background picker does.
- **Eyedropper:** for non-element picker types, [LayerUI.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/LayerUI.tsx) skips editing elements and calls `onSelect`. For the grid, `onSelect` is `setAppState({ gridColor })`, so the eyedropper sets only the grid color.
- **Escape key:** I'll check that pressing Escape inside the color picker closes only the popup and not the whole Grid panel. Both the picker and [GridPanel.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx) listen for Escape.

### Design questions before I start

1. **Faint grid below 0.5×.** At 100% zoom, existing renderer code ([staticScene.ts:112, 131](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts#L112)) hides the thin lines when cells are under 10 screen pixels. So below 0.5× (at the default base of 20px) only every 5th (bold) line shows until you zoom in. I'd leave that core rendering code alone, as Issue #57 asks, unless you want it changed.
2. **Linear slider.** A 0.25–8 slider with 0.05 steps puts 1× only about 10% of the way along. The preset buttons make the common values one click. Is a linear scale acceptable?
3. **Custom colors section:** fill it with scene stroke colors (my recommendation) or leave it empty?
4. **Snapshot files:** keep them (my recommendation) or revert them?

Tell me which fixes to go ahead with, and your answers to these questions, and I'll implement only those.

Nothing has been implemented this turn. Here are the answers, what I found in the shape sliders and in how shapes pass data, and the revised plan.

# Your questions

**3. Custom colors section.** Yes, this comes from the existing shape color pickers. When you open the stroke picker for a rectangle, the first row of the popup is **"Most used custom colors"** ([Picker.tsx:181-186](packages/excalidraw/components/ColorPicker/Picker.tsx#L181-L186)). It lists colors used in the drawing that aren't in the standard palette, for example a hex color you typed in earlier.

- The row is filled by `getMostUsedCustomColors(elements, type)` in [colorPickerUtils.ts:52](packages/excalidraw/components/ColorPicker/colorPickerUtils.ts#L52). It reads each element's `strokeColor` (stroke picker) or `backgroundColor` (fill picker).
- The grid isn't an element, so there's nothing grid-specific to scan. That leaves two options:
  - **(a) Show the stroke colors already used in the drawing.** You could match the grid to your shapes' outlines. This is what I'd recommend.
  - **(b) No custom row**, like the canvas background picker.
- Either way, the Colors, Shades, Hex code and eyedropper sections will all be there.

**4. Snapshot files.** These are the five `__snapshots__/*.snap` files: saved expected output for existing tests, which I regenerated. I'll revert all of them along with [gridPanel.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/gridPanel.test.tsx), so every test file goes back to how Issue #56 left it.

- **The catch:** about 133 existing tests compare the full editor state against those snapshots. The state now has six more fields, so those tests will fail until the snapshots are regenerated during your testing run. I'm assuming that's what you want.

# What I found

**Sliders.** Every slider on a rectangle goes through one shared component, [Range.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/Range.tsx):

- Stroke width ([actionProperties.tsx:616](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionProperties.tsx#L616)) uses `Range` with `notches` (preset buttons above the track), `formatValue` and `alwaysShowValue`.
- Opacity ([actionProperties.tsx:871](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionProperties.tsx#L871)) uses `Range` without notches.
- Step sizes are constants in common, e.g. `STROKE_WIDTH_STEP` ([constants.ts:427](packages/common/src/constants.ts#L427)).

My preset buttons were a separate, hand-built component that duplicated this. They'll be replaced by `Range` with `notches`.

**Step size.** I recommend keeping 0.05 rather than 0.1:

- A 0.1 step counted from a 0.25 minimum gives 0.25, 0.35 … 0.95, 1.05. 1×, 2×, 4× and 8× would never be reachable on the slider.
- With 0.05 there are about 1.5px of track per step, which is tight when dragging with a mouse. Arrow keys move exactly 0.05, and the preset buttons hit the round values.

**Places where my code exposes grid fields to code that doesn't need them.** Shape properties follow one pattern:

- An action owns its state change and renders its own control.
- The panel just calls `actionManager.renderAction("changeOpacity")` ([Actions.tsx:189](packages/excalidraw/components/Actions.tsx#L189)).
- The canvas background color picker works the same way ([actionCanvas.tsx:44](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionCanvas.tsx#L44)).

My code breaks this in three places:

1. **[GridPanel.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx) writes state directly** with `setAppState`, including an `updateData` that passes anything straight through to state. The panel component now knows about every grid field.
2. **[points.ts](packages/common/src/points.ts) in `@excalidraw/common`** (low-level geometry helpers) now knows editor setting names like `gridSnapLinked` and `gridSnapScale`.
3. **[binding.ts:847](packages/element/src/binding.ts#L847) in `@excalidraw/element`** reads the editor's grid settings to work out the snap distance. Its function already accepts the grid size from its caller (`opts.gridSize`, used at [line 779](packages/element/src/binding.ts#L779)); one caller just doesn't pass it.

Two things are already correctly scoped and stay as they are:

- The renderer's state slice (`StaticCanvasAppState`) gets only the four visual fields (`gridScale`, `gridColor`, `gridOpacity`, `gridLayer`). The snap settings aren't exposed to it.
- The grid on/off switches stay as the existing #56 actions.

# Revised plan (awaiting your go)

**Step 1 — Revert the test files.** `git checkout` [gridPanel.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/gridPanel.test.tsx) and the five `.snap` files.

**Step 2 — Move the grid settings into actions, matching how shape properties work.**

- **New [actions/actionGridAppearance.tsx](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionGridAppearance.tsx)** with six actions: `changeGridScale`, `toggleGridSnapLink`, `changeGridSnapScale`, `changeGridColor`, `changeGridOpacity`, `changeGridLayer`.
  - **Each action has:**
    - `perform`, which changes only its own field and uses `captureUpdate: EVENTUALLY` (same as the grid toggles, so these aren't undo steps).
    - `PanelComponent`, which renders the control.
    - `predicate: props.gridModeEnabled === undefined`, copied from [actionToggleGridMode.tsx](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionToggleGridMode.tsx). This hides the controls when the host app controls the grid itself.
  - **What it does on unlink:** `toggleGridSnapLink` copies `gridScale` into `gridSnapScale` when unlinking, so snapping doesn't jump. This keeps the logic you already approved.
- **Register the names:** add them to `ActionName` in [actions/types.ts](packages/excalidraw/actions/types.ts) and export them from [actions/index.ts](packages/excalidraw/actions/index.ts).
- **[GridPanel.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.tsx)** now only handles layout: `actionManager.renderAction("changeGridScale")` and so on. Its `setAppState` calls, the pass-through `updateData`, `GridScaleSelection`, and the options and color constants all go away.
- **Resulting chain:** panel → action manager → `action.perform` → state → canvas redraws ([StaticCanvas.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/canvases/StaticCanvas.tsx) → [staticScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts)) and the snap distance updates (`App.getEffectiveGridSize()`).

**Step 3 — One slider definition for grid size and snap distance.**

- **One small `GridScaleRange` inside the new action file**, used by both scale actions, so the scale settings are defined once.
  - It renders the shared `Range` with `min=MIN_GRID_SCALE` (0.25), `max=MAX_GRID_SCALE` (8) and `step=GRID_SCALE_STEP` (0.05).
  - Preset buttons: 0.25×, 0.5×, 1×, 2×, 4×, 8×.
  - `formatValue` shows "1.35×", and `alwaysShowValue` is on.
  - `onChange` rounds the value to 2 decimals.
- **Opacity** uses `Range` the same way the shape opacity slider does, with its preset step.
- **[constants.ts](packages/common/src/constants.ts):** `MAX_GRID_SCALE` goes from 4 to 8, and I add `GRID_SCALE_STEP = 0.05` next to `STROKE_WIDTH_STEP`. The restore clamp ([normalize.ts:25](packages/excalidraw/scene/normalize.ts#L25) → [restore.ts:1259](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts#L1259)) picks up the new limit automatically.

**Step 4 — Fix the invisible slider.**

- The slider track's gradient uses `--button-bg` ([Range.tsx:70](packages/excalidraw/components/Range.tsx#L70)), which is only defined inside the properties panel (`.App-menu__left`, [styles.scss:732-742](packages/excalidraw/css/styles.scss#L732-L742)).
- I'll define it on `.GridPanel` in [GridPanel.scss](packages/excalidraw/components/GridPanel.scss), with the same light and dark values.
- I'll also style the text preset buttons ("0.25×") to size to their content, and widen the panel to about 16rem so six presets fit on one row.

**Step 5 — Full color picker.**

- `changeGridColor`'s `PanelComponent` renders `ColorPicker` without `palette={null}`. That gives the same Picker the stroke color uses: palette, shades, hex code and eyedropper. Gradient stays off because `allowGradient` defaults to false.
- For the custom colors row, depending on your answer to question 3: with **(a)** I change [Picker.tsx:79](packages/excalidraw/components/ColorPicker/Picker.tsx#L79) so `gridColor` reads element stroke colors; with **(b)** I leave that line as it is.
- I'll also check that Escape inside the picker closes only the popup, not the Grid panel.

**Step 6 — Narrow what each package knows about the grid settings.**

- Move `getGridSpacing` and `getGridSnapSpacing` out of [common/points.ts](packages/common/src/points.ts) into [excalidraw/snapping.ts](packages/excalidraw/snapping.ts), next to `isGridModeEnabled` and `isGridSnapEnabled`.
  - Callers: `App.getEffectiveGridSize()` (snapping) and [staticScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticScene.ts) (spacing of the drawn grid).
  - The two `@excalidraw/common` packages go back to not knowing about grid settings.
- **[binding.ts:847](packages/element/src/binding.ts#L847):** use `opts?.gridSize`, falling back to `appState.gridSize`, which keeps the old behavior for any caller that doesn't pass a size.
  - [App.tsx:9822](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L9822) will pass `gridSize: this.getEffectiveGridSize()`, like the other callers already do (e.g. [linearElementEditor.ts:2217](packages/element/src/linearElementEditor.ts#L2217)).
  - The element package then only ever receives a ready-made pixel distance and never sees the grid scale settings.

**Step 7 — Check everything without adding tests.** Run typecheck, ESLint and Prettier. I'll also run the existing suite once to confirm the only failures are the expected snapshot ones from Step 1.

  T extends Action<TData> = Action<TData>,
>(
  action: T,
) => {
  actions = actions.concat(action);
  return action as T & {
    keyTest?: unknown extends T["keyTest"] ? never : T["keyTest"];
  };
};

import {
  COLOR_PALETTE,
  DEFAULT_ELEMENT_STROKE_COLOR_PALETTE,
  DEFAULT_GRID_COLOR,
  GRID_SCALE_STEP,
  MAX_GRID_SCALE,
  MIN_GRID_SCALE,
} from "@excalidraw/common";

import { CaptureUpdateAction } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { ColorTuple } from "@excalidraw/common";

import { ColorPicker } from "../components/ColorPicker/ColorPicker";
import { RadioSelection } from "../components/RadioSelection";
import { Range } from "../components/Range";
import { BringToFrontIcon, SendToBackIcon } from "../components/icons";
import { t } from "../i18n";
import { getNormalizedGridOpacity, getNormalizedGridScale } from "../scene";

import { register } from "./register";

import type { RangeNotch } from "../components/Range";
import type { AppState } from "../types";

const GRID_COLOR_PICKS = [
  DEFAULT_GRID_COLOR,
  COLOR_PALETTE.gray[3],
  COLOR_PALETTE.red[1],
  COLOR_PALETTE.green[1],
  COLOR_PALETTE.blue[1],
] as ColorTuple;

/**
 * Grid and snapping sizes are multipliers of the base `gridSize`, so the
 * visible grid itself is the reference instead of exact pixel counts.
 */
const GRID_SCALE_PRESETS = [MIN_GRID_SCALE, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, MAX_GRID_SCALE];

const formatGridScale = (value: number) => `${value}×`;

/** shared slider (with presets) for the grid size and the snap distance */
const GridScaleRange = ({
  label,
  value,
  onChange,
  testId,
}: {
  label: string;
  value: number;
  onChange: (value: number) => void;
  testId: string;
}) => (
  <div className="GridPanel__scale">
    <Range
      label={label}
      value={value}
      onChange={onChange}
      min={MIN_GRID_SCALE}
      max={MAX_GRID_SCALE}
      step={GRID_SCALE_STEP}
      minLabel={formatGridScale(MIN_GRID_SCALE)}
      formatValue={formatGridScale}
      alwaysShowValue
      testId={testId}
      notches={GRID_SCALE_PRESETS.map(
        (scale): RangeNotch => ({
          value: scale,
          icon: <span>{formatGridScale(scale)}</span>,
          label: formatGridScale(scale),
          testId: `${testId}-${scale}`,
        }),
      )}
    />
  </div>
);

export const actionChangeGridScale = register<AppState["gridScale"]>({
  name: "changeGridScale",
  label: "labels.gridScale",
  trackEvent: false,
  perform: (elements, appState, value) => {
    return {
      appState: { ...appState, gridScale: getNormalizedGridScale(value) },
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY,
    };
  },
  PanelComponent: ({ appState, updateData }) => (
    <GridScaleRange
      label={t("labels.gridScale")}
      value={appState.gridScale}
      onChange={updateData}
      testId="grid-scale"
    />
  ),
});

export const actionToggleGridSnapLink = register({
  name: "toggleGridSnapLink",
  label: "labels.linkGridSnapScale",
  trackEvent: false,
  perform(elements, appState) {
    const gridSnapLinked = !this.checked!(appState);
    return {
      appState: {
        ...appState,
        gridSnapLinked,
        // start from the current grid size so snapping doesn't jump
        gridSnapScale: gridSnapLinked
          ? appState.gridSnapScale
          : appState.gridScale,
      },
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY,
    };
  },
  checked: (appState) => appState.gridSnapLinked,
});

export const actionChangeGridSnapScale = register<AppState["gridSnapScale"]>({
  name: "changeGridSnapScale",
  label: "labels.gridSnapScale",
  trackEvent: false,
  perform: (elements, appState, value) => {
    return {
      appState: { ...appState, gridSnapScale: getNormalizedGridScale(value) },
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY,
    };
  },
  PanelComponent: ({ appState, updateData }) => (
    <GridScaleRange
      label={t("labels.gridSnapScale")}
      value={appState.gridSnapScale}
      onChange={updateData}
      testId="grid-snap-scale"
    />
  ),
});

export const actionChangeGridColor = register<
  Partial<Pick<AppState, "gridColor" | "openPopup">>
>({
  name: "changeGridColor",
  label: "labels.gridColor",
  trackEvent: false,
  perform: (elements, appState, value) => {
    // the color picker also opens/closes its popup through here
    return {
      appState: {
        ...appState,
        ...(value?.gridColor !== undefined && { gridColor: value.gridColor }),
        ...(value?.openPopup !== undefined && { openPopup: value.openPopup }),
      },
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY,
    };
  },
  PanelComponent: ({ elements, appState, updateData }) => (
    <fieldset>
      <legend>{t("labels.gridColor")}</legend>
      <ColorPicker
        topPicks={GRID_COLOR_PICKS}
        palette={DEFAULT_ELEMENT_STROKE_COLOR_PALETTE}
        type="gridColor"
        label={t("labels.gridColor")}
        color={appState.gridColor}
        onChange={(gridColor) => updateData({ gridColor })}
        elements={elements}
        appState={appState}
        updateData={updateData}
      />
    </fieldset>
  ),
});

export const actionChangeGridOpacity = register<AppState["gridOpacity"]>({
  name: "changeGridOpacity",
  label: "labels.gridOpacity",
  trackEvent: false,
  perform: (elements, appState, value) => {
    return {
      appState: { ...appState, gridOpacity: getNormalizedGridOpacity(value) },
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY,
    };
  },
  PanelComponent: ({ appState, updateData }) => (
    <Range
      label={t("labels.gridOpacity")}
      value={appState.gridOpacity}
      onChange={updateData}
      min={10}
      max={100}
      step={10}
      testId="grid-opacity"
    />
  ),
});

export const actionChangeGridLayer = register<AppState["gridLayer"]>({
  name: "changeGridLayer",
  label: "labels.gridLayer",
  trackEvent: false,
  perform: (elements, appState, value) => {
    return {
      appState: {
        ...appState,
        gridLayer: value === "above" ? "above" : "below",
      },
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY,
    };
  },
  PanelComponent: ({ appState, updateData }) => (
    <fieldset>
      <legend>{t("labels.gridLayer")}</legend>
      <div className="buttonList">
        <RadioSelection<AppState["gridLayer"]>
          type="button"
          options={[
            {
              value: "below",
              text: t("labels.gridLayerBelow"),
              icon: SendToBackIcon,
              testId: "grid-layer-below",
            },
            {
              value: "above",
              text: t("labels.gridLayerAbove"),
              icon: BringToFrontIcon,
              testId: "grid-layer-above",
            },
          ]}
          value={appState.gridLayer}
          onClick={(value) => updateData(value)}
        />
      </div>
    </fieldset>
  ),
});
